explanation: Fires on a function word that marks the upcoming noun phrase or subject as grammatically plural, before any plural noun appears: plural demonstratives 'these'/'those' (strongest, ~0.65-0.95 of max, highest right after 'are'), the plural copula 'are'/'were' (strong ~0.55-0.75 in existential 'there are/were' and presentational 'here are', and in 'where are'; weaker ~0.25-0.4 after a plural noun or 'we'/'they'; near zero after 'you'), numerals two and above and plural quantifiers like 'a few', 'a couple (of)', 'both', 'many', 'several' (~0.35-0.9), and French plural determiners 'ces'/'des'/'les'. It stays near zero on singular counterparts ('this', 'that', 'is', 'was', 'a', 'one'), on 'some' and 'all', and on the plural noun itself, which gets at most a weak spill-over.
